newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: European Union gives $27.5 million to Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: European Union gives $27.5 million to Nicaragua.

text.p: The European Union (EU) on Saturday signed two contracts with Nicaragua's newly inaugurated government, giving it $27.5 million to bolster its education and judicial systems, an official press release said.
The EU will give $20.6 million to build schools and sporting centres in rural areas, and provide housing and training for teachers in the countryside, the press release said.
"For us the education system is important because it is an investment in capital and with this support we will help our rural teachers," Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said.
The remaining $6.9 million will be used to modernise Nicaragua's judicial system, training judges and building courthouses across the country, the press release said.
Aleman has said his government, which took power on Friday, will make rebuilding Nicaragua's shaky judicial system and pauperised schools among its top priorities.
